quiz_item.question: In Chess Requirement 1, which combination of early moves follows sound opening principles after the game starts?
options: A. Move the rooks pawns (a-pawn and h-pawn) forward two squares, bring the queen out on move two to chase edge pawns, and leave the king uncastled in the center.

B. Contest the central squares (d4, d5, e4, e5) with pawns, develop knights and bishops toward the center without moving the same piece repeatedly, and castle early to tuck the king to safety and connect the rooks.
C. Advance the king up the board on move three to lead the attack before moving any knights or bishops off the back rank.
D. Move every pawn forward one square across all eight files before developing a single minor piece.
choices: A. Move the rooks pawns (a-pawn and h-pawn) forward two squares, bring the queen out on move two to chase edge pawns, and leave the king uncastled in the center.

B. Contest the central squares (d4, d5, e4, e5) with pawns, develop knights and bishops toward the center without moving the same piece repeatedly, and castle early to tuck the king to safety and connect the rooks.
C. Advance the king up the board on move three to lead the attack before moving any knights or bishops off the back rank.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Contest the central squares (d4, d5, e4, e5) with pawns, develop knights and bishops toward the center without moving the same piece repeatedly, and castle early to tuck the king to safety and connect the rooks.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Classic chess opening strategy prioritizes controlling the center, developing minor pieces (knights and bishops) efficiently once each, avoiding premature queen excursions, and castling early for king safety.
